record.paper_title: Open Problems on Eigenvalues of the Laplacian
record.original_question: Let Ω be a smooth bounded domain in ℝⁿ, and let 0 = μ₀ < μ₁ ≤ μ₂ ≤ ··· be the Neumann eigenvalues of the Laplacian, defined by −Δv = μv in Ω with ∂v/∂n = 0 on ∂Ω. Must the reciprocal sum |Ω|^{-2/n}(1/μ₁ + ··· + 1/μₙ) be at least the n-ball value n/(C_n^{2/n} p_{n/2,1}²), where p_{ν,1} is the first positive zero of the derivative of t^{1−ν}J_ν(t)? In dimension 2, this is the question whether (1/A)(1/μ₁ + 1/μ₂) ≥ [(1/A)(1/μ₁ + 1/μ₂)]_disk = 2/(π p_{1,1}²).

evidence.quote: Show that (36) holds for an arbitrary smooth bounded domain Ω ⊂ ℝ², and, more generally, show |Ω|^{-2/n}(1/μ₁ + ··· + 1/μₙ) ≥ [|Ω|^{-2/n}(1/μ₁ + ··· + 1/μₙ)]|n-ball = n/(C_n^{2/n} p²_{n/2,1}).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ be a smooth bounded domain, and let
$$0=\mu_0<\mu_1\le\mu_2\le\cdots$$
denote the Neumann eigenvalues of the Laplacian on $\Omega$, i.e. the values $\mu$ for which there exists a nontrivial function $v$ satisfying $-\Delta v=\mu v$ in $\Omega$ and $\partial v/\partial n=0$ on $\partial\Omega$. Write $|\Omega|$ for the Lebesgue measure of $\Omega$, let $C_n=\pi^{n/2}/\Gamma(n/2+1)$ denote the volume of the unit ball in $\mathbb{R}^n$, and let $p_{\nu,1}$ denote the first positive zero of the derivative of $t^{1-\nu}J_\nu(t)$, where $J_\nu$ is the Bessel function of the first kind of order $\nu$.

Prove or disprove the following sharp isoperimetric inequality:
$$|\Omega|^{-2/n}\left(\frac{1}{\mu_1}+\frac{1}{\mu_2}+\cdots+\frac{1}{\mu_n}\right)\ \ge\ \frac{n}{C_n^{2/n}\,p_{n/2,1}^{\,2}},$$
with equality (in the limiting sense) when $\Omega$ is a ball. In particular, in dimension $n=2$, prove or disprove that for every smooth bounded planar domain of area $A$,
$$\frac{1}{A}\left(\frac{1}{\mu_1}+\frac{1}{\mu_2}\right)\ \ge\ \frac{2}{\pi\,p_{1,1}^{\,2}}.$$
artifact.status_search_result: Web search indicates this isoperimetric lower bound for the reciprocal sum of the first n nonzero Neumann eigenvalues remains open in general. Partial results exist (e.g. sharp bounds for the harmonic mean of low Neumann eigenvalues for simply connected planar domains, due to work in the Ashbaugh–Benguria line), but the inequality is not established for arbitrary smooth bounded planar domains or in higher dimensions.

status_evidence.title: Some inequalities involving eigenvalues of the Neumann Laplacian
status_evidence.snippet: Sharp lower bounds for sums of reciprocals of low Neumann eigenvalues for certain classes of domains.
status_evidence.claim: Sharp bounds known in restricted settings; general case open.

status_evidence.title: Dirichlet and Neumann Eigenvalue Problems on Domains in Euclidean Spaces
status_evidence.snippet: Surveys universal and isoperimetric bounds for Neumann eigenvalues including reciprocal sums.
status_evidence.claim: The proposed n-ball lower bound for the reciprocal sum is conjectural in general.
